question.problem: Which of the following gives the arc length of the polar curve $r=\theta +\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta $ for $0\le \theta \le \frac{\pi }{2}?$
question.worked_solution:
The arc length $L$ of a polar curve $r=r(\theta )$ is given by

$$
L={\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}\sqrt{{r}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta })}^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta .
$$

Since $r=\theta +\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,$ we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta }=1-\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta .
$$

Therefore, the arc length is

$$
\begin{aligned}L & ={\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}\sqrt{{r}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta })}^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\sqrt{(\theta +\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta )^{2}+(1-\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\sqrt{({\theta }^{2}+2\theta \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta +{cos}^{2}⁡\theta )+(1-2\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta +{sin}^{2}⁡\theta )}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\sqrt{{\theta }^{2}+2(\theta \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta -\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )+2}\,\text{d}\theta \,.\end{aligned}
$$
